note: Curated from the Btown Brief newsletter vault (editions Jul 31 - Sep 25, 2026). TALKING-POINTS.md is the style doctrine; refreshes land as PRs and points age out via 'added'.

points.text: South Burlington finally broke ground on a bike and pedestrian bridge over I-89, more than five years after it was first proposed — it'll link Staples Plaza to the University Mall by 2028, and it still doesn't have a name. What would you call it?

Vermont Green FC beat the Flint City Bucks to become the first club in USL League Two history to repeat as national champions, closing out an 18-0-1 season and a 42-match unbeaten streak. Which fits Burlington better these days: scrappy underdog, or team we now expect to win it all?

A gram of weed averages $9.59 in Vermont versus $3.87 just over the border in Massachusetts — Vermont capped grow sizes on purpose to keep small farms in business instead of big multistate operators. Worth the markup, or are you making the drive to Massachusetts?

Three homeschooled brothers — 13-year-old twins and their 14-year-old brother — run Black Ice Premium Ice Cream in Essex Junction entirely on their own now, no help from Dad required. What were you running solo at 13?

Sweetwaters just reopened in its old bank building on Church Street after four years dark, chicken fingers and Shirt Sleeve wrap intact — though the 1981 mural of Bernie Sanders is still tiled over underneath. What Burlington spot would you want back exactly as it was?
Rental e-bikes are back on Burlington streets with a 40-mile range, enough to ride the causeway, catch the ferry and loop through South Hero before heading home. Where would your ride end up?
Nearly 14,000 readers cast 300,000 votes in this year's Seven Daysies, crowning Honey Road best restaurant and La Di Da best new restaurant. Who would've gotten your vote?

Vermont rolled out its first ever dedicated tourism brand this month, 'State of Inspiration,' with a hand-drawn logo where the M is shaped like Camel's Hump. Best pitch for out-of-towners, or too cute by half?

Essex's Vermont Ninja Warrior Training Center has three of its own competing on this season of American Ninja Warrior, out of 300 students training there weekly starting at age four. What obstacle would wreck you first?

The Champlain Valley Dinner Train now rolls all the way to Middlebury, with a four-cook kitchen car plating nearly 170 three-course dinners on a single three-hour run. Would you rather work that galley, or just be the guest at table six?
The old Cosmic Grind storefront on Church Street is becoming Artemus Café and Burlington Art Mini Museum, pouring coffee next to local art sold on a sliding scale. Coffee first, or the gallery first?

Sneakers Bistro, a Winooski breakfast and lunch staple since 1980, just opened Sneakeasy, an upstairs cocktail lounge with a clarified Bloody Mary martini. Which meal do you think Sneakers does better: brunch, or last call?
Winooski's Harmony Edosomwan, who cooks traditional Black Southern food at her own Harmony's Kitchen, just won the national Miss Black USA title. What's on your must-try list there?

For the second year running, a herd of GPS-collared goats and sheep called the Chew Crew is munching poison ivy and goldenrod off Jay Peak's ski trails. Goats on payroll — genius, or just funny to picture?

Burlington High School's new building has finally opened after nearly six years in a windowless downtown Macy's — kids on the first tours kept coming back to the natural light. What's the strangest place you've ever gone to school or work?

Retired Shelburne teacher Joplin Wistar has spent retirement building whimsical landmarks around town for free — a backyard hobbit hole, a river troll guarding a footbridge, a 16-foot wooden wind god. Which one would you detour to go see?
An Indeed study just ranked Burlington the third best US city to work in, behind only Boston and Washington DC. Which surprised you more: that we beat San Francisco, or that we beat San Jose?

Vermont's bear population has more than tripled over fifty years to as many as 8,900 bears, nearly double the state's own target. Ever had a bear encounter of your own, or just paranoid about the bird feeder?

The Upper Valley's two-decade-old town listservs — the ones that once matched a kidney donor with a recipient — nearly shut down before a resident-led nonprofit stepped in to save them. What's the most unlikely thing you've seen solved on a local listserv or Front Porch Forum?

VTrans says the wobble you feel on I-89 between Montpelier and St. Albans has an actual name: raveling, when the top layer of pavement disintegrates entirely. Did you already have your own name for that stretch of road?

A Burlington boat captain's sonar turned up a 100-to-200-yard chain of tires strung together on the bottom of Lake Champlain's Cumberland Bay, arranged like a breakwater nobody remembers building — and weeks later, they're still down there. What's your best theory for how they got there?

After nearly ten years of work, Burlington's ten-mile Wildways Trail is officially finished, linking the Intervale, Ethan Allen Homestead, Ethan Allen Park and Rock Point into one continuous route from the Winooski River to the lake. Which stretch would you walk first?

The Peace & Justice Center hid 33 clusters of tiny blue peace-sign stickers across 24 Burlington parks this summer, with clues written as poems — so far exactly one person has found all 33. Which park would you start your hunt in?

Vermont's nesting loon population has climbed from about 15 pairs in the 1990s to 115 last year, credited to nesting rafts, education and a ban on lead sinkers — and two chicks hatched on Hinesburg's Lake Iroquois this summer under a volunteer's watch. Where's the best spot you've heard a loon call?

VTrans just put the 359-foot Burlington-Winooski Bridge — built in 1928 — up for free on Craigslist, since federal rules require historic bridges to be offered away before they're torn down; whoever takes it has to haul it off in pieces themselves. So far the only reply asked, 'Can I move it tomorrow?' What would you actually do with a free, near-century-old bridge?

A flock of sheep escaped from the Episcopal Diocese down the street and wandered the new Burlington High School's grounds Monday before diocese staff rounded them up and walked them home. What's the strangest animal you've bumped into somewhere around town?
